Hi Jamie / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the specific follow-ups you asked for on pricing and unit economics so your finance/product partners can model this into Q4 planning.

Key takeaways from our side:
- Scope: Care+ feature set — prioritizing in-chat summarization + automated care-plan drafts for high-risk patients. Estimated 40k monthly active users (MAU) for initial pilot across 3k clinicians.
- Usage profile: expected 1.2M–1.8M tokens/month in pilot (mostly generation; average response ~650 tokens; peak concurrency nominal).
- Your budget anchor: you mentioned a target inference line-item of approximately $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens in early procurement discussions.

Requested items (we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow):
1) A conservative per-feature unit economics worksheet ($/feature per MAU / month) using the token ranges you provided.
2) Pricing band options (hosted vs. reserved/dedicated) and expected per-1M-token bill for pilot volumes.
3) Simple CAC payback scenarios assuming 1) low uplift (net +$8/mo per user), 2) mid (+$15/mo), 3) high (+$28/mo).

Next step from you: confirm whether the 1.2M–1.8M tokens/month is the most likely pilot range, or whether we should model a higher conservative cap (2.5M). Also, if procurement will require a formal SOW/MA with the finance team looped in (cc’ing procurement helps).

I’m looping Ben (pricing) and Marissa (customer success) so we can get you the worksheet + recommended pricing bands.

Subject: internal: SY-3482 quick unit-econ sketch for Synergy Health

Internal note — working through the numbers Jamie provided. I sketched a concise worksheet (will attach final) and a few assumptions below so we can align on the message to Synergy procurement:

Assumptions (pilot baseline = 1.25M tokens):
- Token mix: 85% generation, 15% embeddings/rerank.
- Average tokens per feature invocation: 650 tokens (generation only).
- Feature invocations/month per clinician (active): 35 -> tokens per clinician/month ~22.8k -> at 3k clinicians this is ~68.4M tokens if applied to all clinicians. BUT Synergy clarified only subset of clinicians will use Care+ in pilot; we'll model per-MAU (40k MAU is likely org-wide; pilot MAU = 1.25M tokens/650 ~1.9k feature invocations -> implies ~55 clinicians active). We'll surface both per-MAU and scaled scenarios.

Redwood indicative pricing bands (net unit price to Synergy before any negotiated discount):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): list $1,200 / 1M tokens; typical early-stage discounting to $1,000–$1,050 for pilot volumes and trial credits.
- Dedicated (12mo reserved): effective $600 / 1M tokens at committed throughput with a standard reserved uplift.

Per-feature cost (per active clinician per month) at 1.25M tokens pilot (modeling per-MAU):
- Tokens consumed per active clinician (pilot): ~22.8k tokens -> per-feature inference cost at hosted $1,000 / 1M = $22.8k * $1,000 / 1,000,000 = $22.80 -> round to $23/clinician/mo.
- At reserved $600 / 1M -> $13.68 -> round $14/clinician/mo.

CAC payback: using CAC $180
- Conservative uplift $12/mo -> payback at hosted price: CAC / (uplift - incremental infra cost) = 180 / (12 - 23) -> negative (loss), meaning at hosted list/early discounted price the uplift does not cover per-user inference cost. With reserved pricing: 180 / (12 - 14) -> still negative (loss). So for a $12 uplift, economics don't work at this activation density unless we reduce per-feature cost via caching, batching, or smaller model variant.
- Mid uplift $15/mo -> Hosted: 180 / (15 - 23) -> negative; Reserved: 180 / (15 - 14) = 180 months (~15 years) -> meaningless.
- Optimistic uplift $20/mo -> Hosted: 180 / (20 - 23) -> negative; Reserved: 180 / (20 - 14) = 30 months -> 2.5 years.

Findings / implications:
1) At the current average tokens/invocation and the uplift ranges Jamie shared, per-clinician economics do not reach standard SaaS payback targets unless: a) Synergy targets higher uplift / monetization per clinician OR b) we materially lower inference cost via reserved commitment, model/quantization choice, or reduce tokens per invocation (summaries 350–400 tokens).
2) Quick levers to propose to procurement: smaller model with same perceived quality for summaries, off-peak batching, or quota-based routing to cheaper model variants for low-risk patients.

I'll finalize the worksheet and attach a version with shaded cells for ranges (1.0M / 1.25M / 1.5M tokens) + a recommendation slide that shows the narrative: "reserved commitment + model optimization required to reach >12 month payback at realistic uplifts."

Ben
Director, Pricing & Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

Hi Jamie / Alex —

Thanks again for the clarity on volumes and procurement targets. Attached is a concise packet:
- SY-3482-Unit-Econ.xlsx (tabbed: Summary, 1.0/1.25/1.5M scenarios, Payback Sensitivity).
- Redwood-pricing-band.pdf (hosted vs reserved illustrative bands).

Top-line recommendations (short):
1) If Synergy wants payback <12 months at realistic uplifts ($12–$20/mo), we recommend a 12-month reserved commitment (targeting effective $550–$650 / 1M tokens) plus a 10%–20% engineering optimization target (reduce avg tokens/invocation to ~420–500).
2) If procurement cannot commit to reserved, explore a limited pilot discount + guardrails (rate-limited per-invocation, caching) and push product to instrument finer-grained usage controls so you can run a small profitable cohort.
3) We are happy to run an A/B on a lower-cost model variant (quantized) for 50% of traffic to measure any quality delta; that often bridges the economics without impacting clinician-facing UX.

Questions for procurement: what flexibility is there on a 12-month commitment vs a 6-month with capacity step-ups? Also please confirm the finance contact we should prepare the SOW for (we'll populate the legal/pricing annex once capacity/commitment terms are agreed).

Attaching the workbook and the short pricing band PDF for procurement review.
